prediction.whatIsNeededForEstimate: To convert this into a real dollar range we would need: (1) Omega's market capitalization and average daily trading volume during the relevant disclosure windows (July 27 and October 31, 2017); (2) an expert-constructed event study or 'inflation ribbon' isolating the portion of the 4% and 6.8% stock price declines attributable to the alleged fraud versus general market/sector movement; (3) the number of shares purchased by class members during the May 3-October 31, 2017 class period and their purchase prices (to compute per-share out-of-pocket or Section 21D damages); and (4) if this were instead being valued for settlement purposes, comparable information about any settlement demand or mediator's proposal, none of which appears in the motion-to-dismiss opinion provided.
prediction.likelyOutcome: The § 10(b)/Rule 10b-5 omission theory (non-disclosure of the working capital loan), paired with strong circumstantial scienter allegations and concrete loss-causation stock-drop evidence, is likely to survive the motion to dismiss in whole or substantial part, with the § 20(a) control-person claims following it; the separate FFO/AFFO misstatement theory is a closer call because of the GAAP-violation pleading gap, and some individual forward-looking or puffery statements will likely be dismissed as non-actionable even if the core case proceeds. Because this is a merits opinion at the motion-to-dismiss stage with no damages model, market-cap data, or settlement figure in the record, no dollar recovery range can be responsibly computed yet.

outcome.description: After the district court dismissed the first amended complaint in 2019, the Second Circuit reversed in 2020 (968 F.3d 204), holding the non-disclosure of the working capital loan to the operator actionable and scienter adequately pleaded. On remand the court largely denied a renewed motion to dismiss (Sept. 28, 2021). The parties then settled; the court granted preliminary approval on December 27, 2022, and on April 25, 2023 entered an Order and Final Judgment approving a $30,750,000 cash settlement for the class of Omega securities purchasers (https://storage.courtlistener.com/recap/gov.uscourts.nysd.484014/gov.uscourts.nysd.484014.167.0.pdf). Attorneys' fees were paid out of the settlement fund.
outcome.finalNote: Court-approved class settlement of $30.75 million (S.D.N.Y. Order and Final Judgment, ECF No. 167, April 25, 2023); fees came out of the fund; no appeal of the settlement.
